scope: Reference Nginx forwarding authority, routing, response controls, request ceiling, outer rate budget, and two-upstream distribution
sourceState: uncommitted working tree; no repository commit exists

priorDefect.failureMode: The public API edge preserved a client-selected forwarding prefix. Because Fastify trusted the direct Nginx peer, a caller could influence the proxy-resolved client address used by the distributed limiter and split the application budget. The catch-all web route also passed client forwarding metadata through unchanged.

negativeSelfTests: an additional $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for directive is rejected even when the required overwrite remains present
an additional copied $http_forwarded directive is rejected even when the required removal remains present

limitations: The verifier uses one host and loopback HTTP; it does not prove TLS, external load balancers, multi-host scheduling, production network policy, or the exact production binary.

Two real Fastify instances validate proxy-address semantics, but the full ReconAI API, Redis application limiter, authenticated routes, and Next.js runtime are not composed in this edge-only exercise.
The observed burst is a bounded control test, not representative capacity, latency, availability, or denial-of-service resistance evidence.
No customer payload, production credential, staging deployment, external alert, or hosted CI run is included.
remainingEvidenceAndOperationalRisks: Repeat the forwarding-authority and routing proof through every actual ingress and load-balancer hop with exact approved direct-peer CIDRs.
Run the edge and application budgets together in a multi-replica staging topology against representative burst, sustained, multi-address, authentication, webhook, and expensive-route load.
Exercise Redis startup loss, runtime loss, recovery, HMAC-key rotation, readiness polling, and alert delivery through the deployed topology.
Verify TLS termination, request timeout behavior, network policy, scheduler behavior, and version-hidden error responses at the deployed edge.
